task:
Galaxy map: viewport-aware catalogue star streaming with stable spatial cells and reserved slots for important systems (map review finding M08). apps/web only; no API change.

VERIFIED ON MAIN (dd45ee34): `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/galaxy-star-stream.ts` `galaxyStarViewport()` builds the local request as a box of fixed multipliers around the focus (horizontal radius min(7,400, 0.82·distance), vertical min(3,000, 0.34·distance)) regardless of viewport aspect, bearing or pitch; Explore applies an additional circular XZ filter; above the local band the request is a fixed whole-galaxy box. At shallow pitch or wide aspect the visible footprint exceeds the box; off-screen points consume the budget; the native V3 path orders by id64 so which stars appear depends on id order, not relevance.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Footprint: derive the request bounds from the camera's actual view — intersect the frustum (use `galaxyCameraPose` / the pose helpers in `galaxy-camera.ts`) with the galactic plane band around the focus Y, take its XZ bounding box with an overscan margin (e.g. 15%), clamp to the existing 15,000 LY API cube bound and the catalogue bounds. Keep the Y band as today. Keep the per-band budgets from `galaxy-detail-policy.ts`.
2. Stable cells: quantise the footprint to a grid of spatial cells (cell size a function of the detail band, e.g. 250 / 1,000 / 2,500 LY) and request whole cells, so small camera moves reuse cached cells (tanstack query keyed by cell) instead of refetching a slightly shifted box. Keep a bounded LRU of cells around the camera (e.g. 64 cells) and evict the farthest first.
3. Reserved slots: before sampling background detail, guarantee that the selected system, the search anchor/reference, the current Finder results and the user's pins/watchlist systems (when present in the page) are included in the rendered catalogue set even if the viewport sample would not return them (merge their known positions; mark them as `reserved` in the contribution so the renderer can prefer them in picking). Do not invent population or brightness.
4. Keep the API request shape (`/api/map/systems` viewport query) and its `limit`; only the bounds and the client-side assembly change. The circular XZ filter in Explore is replaced by the footprint test (a point is kept if inside the requested footprint polygon with margin).
5. Do not change thresholds, materials or the detail policy constants.

TESTS (vitest): footprint bounds at pitch 0.2 / 0.8 / top-down and aspect 1:1 / 21:9 contain the projected corners of the visible plane region and respect the cube bound; cell quantisation returns the same cell set for a 5% camera shift and a different set for a 100% shift; LRU eviction order; reserved systems always present in the assembled contribution with `reserved: true`; the footprint filter keeps on-screen points and drops off-screen ones at shallow pitch. Existing star-stream, policy and workspace tests must keep passing; update the ones pinning the old box multipliers and say so in CHANGES.md.

VALIDATION: in apps/web `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. CHANGES.md: one dated 2026-11-02 entry; note the visible map change needs Product E2E/visual validation before production promotion and is not deployed.
